title: Sutrakritanga
attributionNote: Traditionally the teaching of Mahāvīra transmitted by Sudharman, in whose voice the dialogue is spoken. The second book is generally held to be the later of the two.
description: The second Aṅga of the Śvetāmbara canon, in two books: sixteen lectures on the doctrine and on the refutation of rival teachers — the Kriyāvādins, Akriyāvādins, Ajñānikas and Vinayavādins — and seven on activity, food, the renunciation of activity, freedom from error and the debates at Nālandā. It is the canon's principal work of argument, and a principal source for what early Jain authors knew of other schools.
historicalContext: The Sūtrakṛtāṅga preserves one of the oldest Jain accounts of the philosophical landscape of northern India, classifying and answering the fatalists, the eternalists and the sceptics. Its second book, with the Nālandā debates, is later in style and doctrine than the first.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive view by view at read time. Jacobi's 1895 translation is public domain; the Prakrit text is not included.
